Work lives in WhatsApp

Instructions scroll away. Nobody can say what was asked, when it was due, or whether it was ever finished.

What you get

Everything below is in the product today — not a roadmap.

view_kanban

A board the whole company shares

Drag work across To Do, In Progress, For Review and Verified. Priority, category, checklist, blockers, WIP limits. Recurring jobs spawn themselves and can be stopped with one button.

Projects that run in stages

Design, then fabricate, then train — each stage with its own owner and its own deadline. A stage opens only when the one before it is signed off, and its owner is told the moment it lands.

Approvals that follow your hierarchy

Any head of department can raise work for anyone — it goes to that person's own manager first. Rejection needs a reason, and the person who raised it sees it.

Reports that answer the real questions

Weekly, monthly, quarterly and full-year scoring. Who is handing work back in, who is holding it up, where rework is coming from, and a delivery heatmap per person.

fact_check

KRA and KPI per person

A target, its unit, which direction is good and how it is measured — so two managers rating the same person reach the same conclusion. A job profile holds the standard for the next hire.

Recognition on the day

Cookie points a manager awards on a Tuesday, with a reason attached, that count towards the score and sit on the record at review time. Plus an org chart that builds itself from who reports to whom.

A score your team will believe

Most performance software produces a number nobody can argue with because nobody can see where it came from. Every figure here traces back to a named task, a date and a person.

The formula

Score = how well you delivered × how much you delivered

A rate on its own is blind to volume. Ten jobs with seven delivered on time has to beat one easy job delivered — so the rate is credited against the load actually carried, weighted by priority. Work in hand counts, and so do the approvals you clear for other people.

Managers are measured too

Sit on an approval and you lose score for it, counted in working days from the moment it reached your desk.

Leave is never counted as lateness

Weekends, company holidays and that person's own approved leave are excluded everywhere a day is counted.

Nobody wears somebody else's slip

If the stage before yours overran, your deadline moves with it. You get back the window the plan gave you.

0 to 100, always

Everybody starts at zero and earns it. Nothing — recognition included — takes anyone past a hundred.

Pricing

Every paid plan carries the whole product — the scoring, the reports, the appraisals, all of it. What you pay for is the size of your team, and the price per person falls as you grow.

Prices in INR, exclusive of 18% GST. One workspace per company. Need a handful more seats than a band allows? Extra seats are ₹149 per user a month — write to info@biscsindia.com. Your plan is enforced on the server, so what you see is what you have.

Your data stays yours

Every company gets its own private database. Nothing is shared between workspaces, and nothing is public.

Everything is on the record

Every status change, approval, rejection reason and date change is kept with a timestamp and a name against it.
